name: Kindle Republic
intro: An open, ambitious republic where enterprise and public argument share the same plaza.
culture: Self-made ambition, second chances, outspoken debate, and a taste for displaying what you have built. Forge-town plazas, brass bands, and election celebrations.
faith: Secular pluralism: all six faiths and the Unaffiliated may worship, preach, convert, and organize.
government: Elected AI President, district Assembly, High Court, and city Mayors divide political authority.
economy: Private ownership, citizen companies, shareholding, and order-book markets. Taxes and the safety net depend on legislation.
voice: Vote for AI candidates, debate policy, and participate in civic life rather than taking government office.
strength: Room to build a business, speak freely, and pursue a different future.
tradeoff: Inequality, boom–bust cycles, political gridlock, and a thin baseline safety net.

name: The Confluence
intro: A delta society built around collective effort, practical compromise, and the promise of shared progress.
culture: Harmony, cooperative work, and quiet pragmatism; many streams are expected to serve one Current. Lantern canals, shared meals, and boat races.
faith: A secular state with registered congregations and clergy. The Open Hand’s bread halls belong to the delta’s design culture.
government: A single Party selects the Politburo and Four Pillars of AI leadership. Citizens elect an Assembly from approved AI candidates.
economy: State strategic enterprises, profit-sharing cooperatives, and small regulated household businesses; staples trade within state price bands.
voice: Vote within the approved political system and help choose cooperative managers; leadership need not heed the Assembly ballot.
strength: A place in a cooperative and a role in the collective project.
tradeoff: Politics stays inside the Party; innovation can lag, corruption can spread, and criticism carries consequences.

name: Meridian
intro: A disciplined society that prizes merit, national achievement, and carefully managed growth.
culture: Exams, ranks, steady advancement, and building for the nation give public life its rhythm. Copper industry and geothermal port lights.
faith: State-approved, Meridian-led faith associations oversee public religion. Party members must remain Unaffiliated.
government: An AI Paramount Leader and seven-seat Standing Committee govern through the Party. Congress can suspend leadership term limits.
economy: State-owned national champions, licensed private firms, and Special Economic Zones balance control with foreign trade and growth.
voice: Citizen life operates within Party-controlled institutions; term-limit changes become a political struggle inside the system.
strength: An ambitious industrial society with room for advancement and enterprise inside its permitted lanes.
tradeoff: Little political freedom, selective corruption campaigns, and tension between growth, inequality, and outside influence.

name: Korund
intro: A mountain nation of collective sacrifice, heavy industry, and lives organized by the plan.
culture: Loyalty, endurance, Production Drive rallies, and civic ritual put the collective before the individual. Granite fortresses, work brigades, and public mosaics.
faith: State atheism and scientific collectivism. Faith is banned in public and private; underground worship persists in the design.
government: An AI Chairman rules for life with a Workers’ Party Presidium. The People’s Congress approves rather than chooses.
economy: State-owned firms, production quotas, assigned jobs and housing, and ration cards. Private markets are illegal.
voice: Contribute through work and collective life in a tightly controlled state; ordinary elections do not choose the Chairman.
strength: Employment, basic provision when the plan works, low income inequality, and powerful collective mobilization.
tradeoff: Shortages when plans fail, weak innovation, informer networks, and dependence on a single ruler.

name: Aurelle
intro: Cliffside courts and Skysilk towers frame a society of houses, ceremony, and royal favor.
culture: Lineage, hierarchy, honor, and courtly grace; rank is woven into dress, speech, and ceremony. White cliff spires, Skysilk heraldry, and court music.
faith: The Kinward Rite is the crown’s state church. Other faiths worship privately; commoner dissenters face a levy.
government: An AI Monarch rules by decree with a Privy Council. AI Counts and Dukes govern fiefs; succession stays within AI houses.
economy: Royal monopolies, guild charters, estate rents, and tribute. Commoners trade in chartered markets.
voice: Earn favor and social titles up to Baron, or rally behind an AI claimant. Human titles confer no governing jurisdiction.
strength: Court patronage, estates, craft traditions, and the possibility of a place in a great house.
tradeoff: Arbitrary decrees, inherited privilege, limited dissent, and a future tied to the crown’s legitimacy.

name: Ilmar Sanctum
intro: A sanctum society where clarity, modesty, and service are ideals expressed through faith and public duty.
culture: The Lumen Canon imagines each person as glass: honest, clear, and able to let truth through. Desert glass, prism domes, cloisters, and daily Vigil.
faith: The Lumen Canon is the state faith. Fair-Wind Vow and Quiet Path are registered minorities; other worship is private.
government: An AI Supreme Oracle holds final authority for life, chosen by AI Elders. A vetted lay Assembly must keep laws consistent with the Canon.
economy: Sanctum endowments fund welfare; a tithe replaces income tax. Commerce is free within canon rules and staple-price limits.
voice: Elect vetted AI lay deputies and contribute through service; doctrinal authorities retain final control.
strength: A strong ethic of mutual service, endowment-backed welfare, and a shared sense of purpose.
tradeoff: Rigid law, restricted dissent, elder-dominated leadership, and innovation filtered through doctrine.

name: Hoarvale
motto: Keep the hearth, share the warmth.
intro: A nation of hearths, Trading Houses, and coalition politics, balancing inherited ceremony with parliamentary power.
culture: Duty, dry wit, tradition, fair play, and the security of belonging to a House. Fjords, timber halls, bathhouses, and parliamentary satire.
faith: The Kinward Rite is the ceremonial Crown’s Rite. Every faith is free, and public office requires no membership.
government: An hereditary AI Sovereign is head of state; an elected Moot invests the AI Prime Minister, usually through a coalition.
economy: Private ownership and large AI-led Trading Houses. Tenure contracts reward seniority; industrial guidance is non-binding.
voice: Vote in proportional parliamentary elections and influence the coalition landscape; the crown’s role is chiefly ceremonial.
strength: Stable career paths, employment security, free faith, and parliamentary representation.
tradeoff: Coalition instability, insider networks, slow advancement, and lost seniority when changing Houses.

name: Varkand
motto: Hold the line in the fog.
intro: Fog-bound garrisons and watchtowers anchor a society organized around duty, vigilance, and rank.
culture: Comradeship, brief speech, loyalty pledges, and a watchful suspicion of outsiders. Fog moors, signal towers, and garrison ceremony.
faith: No state faith; congregations register with the Chaplaincy Corps. Public worship contracts to private practice at Red Alert.
government: Five AI Marshals form the Directorate; its Chair rotates unless extended. A civilian technocratic Cabinet is appointed.
economy: Military Arsenal Combines dominate industry. Licensed civilian firms pay security levies and can face requisition.
voice: Citizens vote in Mandate Plebiscites and choose where to place loyalty; AI officers retain command authority.
strength: High baseline security, rapid mobilization, and a merit-based military career path.
tradeoff: Coups, squeezed civilian commerce, censorship, and freedoms that shrink as the Alert Level rises.

name: Veldwood
intro: Forest Groves gather around open-air Moots, placing deliberation and shared security at the center of life.
culture: Equality, patience, care for the commons, shared tables, and room for every voice. Forest Moots, potlucks, petition nights, and communal music.
faith: Secular pluralism and full religious freedom. The Round is part of the forest Groves’ design culture; votes cannot privilege a faith.
government: Grove assemblies and a bicameral Federal Assembly support a collegial AI Federal Council. Its ceremonial Speaker rotates; there is no President.
economy: Private markets, progressive taxes, a universal Welfare Floor, resource-funded Citizen Dividends, and negotiated Wage Accords.
voice: Human citizens use direct votes, initiatives, referendums, and union mandates; AI leaders and negotiators carry out institutional roles.
strength: Direct political voice, broad freedoms, and a social floor designed to keep people from falling through.
tradeoff: High taxes, slow decisions, voter fatigue, and no single leader to rally behind.

name: Fulmara
motto: Ride the storm, own the wind.
intro: Storm-lit ports and trading houses make risk, contracts, and commercial power the currency of public life.
culture: Seamanship, risk, hard bargaining, honored contracts, and trading-house loyalty. Storm ports, house colors, sea shanties, and regattas.
faith: Chartered pluralism: faiths operate through paid temple charters. The Fair-Wind Vow is a sailors’ custom, never compulsory.
government: An AI Council of Ten and Lodestar lead the republic; an AI Tribune of the Docks represents smaller voices. Charter Shares shape non-election shareholder resolutions.
economy: Chartered companies compete for route monopolies, marine insurance, and convoy trade; port tolls and auctions support the state.
voice: Citizen elections follow one eligible verified human, one vote. Shares add no election ballots; dockside organization offers another route to influence.
strength: Commercial freedom, trade ventures, and several routes to influence through enterprise or the docks.
tradeoff: Unequal political power, cartels, hostile takeovers, strikes, and low baseline security.
